body.en:
Question B-008-001-007.

Why the correct answer is right: The outside gain antenna delivers much stronger off-channel signals to the handheld very-high-frequency (VHF) receiver. Its front end can mix those signals internally, causing receiver intermodulation on the desired frequency.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Harmonics from other stations": Harmonics from other stations would be exact multiples of their frequencies; the mixed modulation heard after adding a gain antenna points to receiver intermodulation.
- sourceIndex 2: "Audio stage overload": Audio-stage overload would occur after detection and would not usually create a mixture of RF signals on the selected frequency.
- sourceIndex 3: "Audio stage intermodulation": Audio-stage intermodulation is the wrong stage; the problem begins when strong RF signals enter the receiver front end.
